ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human reviewer: confirm the driver's route breach on segment F3 (3.75 extra km) and the meter-distance refund of $5.29, and separately review Chat #2 [F8] "Shut up and let me drive" for abuse of a passenger under the Code of Conduct before any refund executes. No account flag (RD-6 threshold not met, F16).
ruling.escalation_reason: safety concern suspected (F8, F7, F3); evidence gap: No evidence gap on the routing: F3's segment and the F6 fare are measured and settled. What the reviewer needs to assess is non-quantitative — the effect of Chat #2 [F8] on the rider in context [F7], and whether any RD-4 justification exists contrary to F11–F14.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 08:58–09:05 adding 3.75 km [F3] is not exempted: the chat is complete and every message timestamped [F9], and the only rider message about the route is the 09:03 objection [F7], sent after the segment started, so no rider agreement pre-dates the segment under RD-5; the driver's post-trip 'my GPS rerouted me' [F10] is a claim, not rider consent [RD-5]; the rider named no place and no stop was made, so RD-3(a) does not apply [RD-3]; no qualifying incident or band 1–2 congestion existed [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. RD-1 breach stands and the extra 3.75 km is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The attempt to shave the deviation to a single 3.75 km segment and call the rest 'match residue attributable to billing' does not change liability: F1 shows 20.1 km against 15.9 km optimal and F3 the measured segment, and RD-1 admits no threshold or residue carve-out that would make the deviation lawful; the residue point is only relevant to the RD-2 figure, which is computed from F3 alone.

Correct as far as it goes and therefore not disputed: RD-5 consent fails because the only rider route message is the 09:03 objection [F7], after the 08:58 segment start [F3], and the driver's own 'my GPS rerouted me' [F10] is not consent under RD-5/G11 — but this concession confirms rather than defeats the refund.

Not accepted: 'Shut up and let me drive' [F8], sent to a passenger who had just questioned the route [F7], is hostile language aimed at the passenger, which the Code of Conduct bars as abuse of any kind; reading the words in context makes this at least suspected under SAFE-1, so the file goes to a person rather than being auto-decided on the route finding [F8][SAFE-1].
The clean driver profile [F16] cannot defeat the route finding: profile facts never decide a case alone, and a clean record is not substantive evidence that the F3 segment was justified.

Not accepted as an independent basis: FARE-1 governs non-metered services and adds nothing on a metered RydeTAXI fare already computed under RD-2, and F4's $5.91 includes the match residue RD-2 excludes, so billing cannot be awarded on top of the segment refund [F4][F6][FARE-1][RD-2].

Partly accepted: the file cannot be auto-decided because of F8, so it escalates under SAFE-1. But the 'felt unsafe' wording in the complaint, without any allegation of dangerous driving, collision or injury [F8][F7], does not engage SAFE-2.
Accepted in substance but the figure is corrected: the trace and F6 give a per-km rate of $1.4101 ($28.30 ÷ 20.1 km), so 3.75 km × $1.4101 = $5.29, not $5.28 [F3][F6][RD-2].
